transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. Thanks for coming in today. Can you tell me what brings you in to see me?

Well... I guess it's because of stuff at my apartment building. The people living around me, they're... they watch my comings and goings. And I know they're slipping notes about me down to the office. Everyone keeps telling me it's just regular notices they tape on the doors, but... I know they're watching me. So that's why I'm here.
How long have you noticed these things happening—when did you first start feeling that your neighbors were watching you and sending notes about you?
I don't know exactly. It's been a while. Just... maybe a year. Yeah, about a year and a month, I guess. That's when I started noticing it.
Besides feeling watched and noticing the notes, have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people don't seem to hear, or seen things others don't see?
No... I don't think so. Just the people watching me. I haven't heard anything like that.
Over this past year, have you had any periods where your mood was very low, hopeless, or unusually high and energetic, separate from your concerns about being watched?

I don't know about energetic... but low, yeah. Most mornings I wake up with this... heavy, hollow feeling. Like the day already went bad before I even get my feet on the floor. It's just... hard to get going.
During times when you're not feeling low or hollow in the morning, do you still find yourself believing your neighbors are watching you and sending notes about you?

Yeah... I mean, there was a... a spell, I guess. A few weeks where I was eating a little better. I wasn't waking up feeling quite so... hopeless. But... yeah, I still knew they were watching my door. They were still reporting on me. That didn't stop just because I felt a little better.
Over the past year, would you say you've felt low or hopeless most of the time, or has that feeling come and gone, with longer stretches where you felt more like your usual self?

Most of the time, yeah. Ever since I moved... it's just been there. Even if I have a day where I can... sound a little clearer, I guess... I still feel pretty low. Just... useless. I don't really care about the things I used to do anymore. So... no, it hasn't really gone away.
Was there ever a stretch of at least two weeks where you felt completely free of that low, hopeless mood, yet you still believed your neighbors were watching and reporting on you?

Yeah... I think I mentioned that already. There was a... a few weeks, maybe. I wasn't waking up feeling quite as bad. Eating a little better. But... yeah, they were still watching. Still keeping track of me. That didn't stop.

Out of this whole year since it started, would you say the low, hollow mood has been present for most of that time, or was that few-week period when you felt a bit better actually a fairly large chunk of the year?

Yeah... like I said... it's been most of the time. Ever since I moved... it's just been there. Even if I have a day where I can... sound a little clearer, I guess... I still feel pretty low. Just... useless. I don't really care about the things I used to do anymore. So... yeah, most of the year.

latest_inference.note: The patient reports persistent persecutory delusions for about a year, with depressive mood present most of that time, but also a distinct several-week period where mood symptoms improved while the delusional beliefs persisted unchanged. This pattern—mood symptoms occupying the majority of the illness duration alongside psychotic symptoms, plus a period of psychotic symptoms without prominent mood disturbance—fits the criteria for schizoaffective disorder rather than a pure delusional disorder, which would not typically feature such prominent, persistent depressive symptoms occupying most of the illness course.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports persistent persecutory delusions (neighbors watching/reporting on him) for approximately 14 months, meeting criterion A for psychotic disorder. Concurrently, he describes a pervasive depressive syndrome (low, hollow mood, anhedonia, hopelessness, feelings of uselessness) present for the majority of this period. Critically, he identifies a discrete few-week period during which his depressive symptoms remitted (better mood, improved appetite) while the persecutory delusions persisted unabated, establishing that psychotic symptoms occurred for at least 2 weeks in the absence of a mood episode (ruling out major depressive disorder with psychotic features). However, the mood symptoms have been present for the majority of the total duration of the illness (most of the year), which is required for schizoaffective disorder rather than schizophrenia with comorbid depression. No manic symptoms were endorsed, and no hallucinations were reported. This pattern—psychotic symptoms with concurrent mood episode for majority of illness duration, plus a period of psychosis without mood disturbance—is most consistent with Schizoaffective Disorder, depressive type (F25.1).
